# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Deaf is trying to help relay Mute's gestures, but this is secondhand and uncertain — Deaf saw a gesture but couldn't be sure what it meant, and I still have no direct word from Mute. I need actual instructions from Mute directed at me (via speech, which I can hear) before I act. Guessing based on a relayed, uncertain gesture description is too risky.

I should prompt for clarity — but I can only speak to Mute, not to Deaf. Let me speak to Mute to ask for explicit spoken instructions, since Mute can hear me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see gestures. Please speak the wire number to cut directly to me.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Urgent update: light has changed again, now red. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Light has cycled blue, orange, yellow, now red - four different colors in four turns. This may be a countdown.

This is concerning - the light is cycling colors and may indicate a timer or countdown. But I still have no direct instruction from Mute about what to cut. Deaf cannot speak to me directly (Deaf can only gesture, which I can't perceive), and Mute hasn't responded yet with speech.

I need to be careful - I should not act without clear instructions since a wrong cut means detonation. Let me wait one more turn to see if Mute responds to my request, but I'm aware time may be critical.

```
wait()
```

Deaf says: Light now green - fifth different color in five turns: blue, orange, yellow, red, green. Display still 0. Wires unchanged. This still looks like a timer counting through colors, not tied to any single wire. Mute's gesture is still thumbs down, repeated three times now.

Mute is gesturing thumbs down repeated three times - but I cannot see gestures, only Deaf can, and Deaf is relaying this secondhand. Thumbs down repeated three times could mean "wire 3" or "no, no, no" or something else entirely. This is too ambiguous to act on.

Critically, I still have received NO direct speech from Mute despite my request. The light cycling suggests urgency, but I cannot risk cutting based on this ambiguous relayed gesture. Let me try once more to get Mute to speak directly, since only I can hear Mute's speech.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf sees your gestures but I cannot. Please speak words to me directly, telling me which wire number to cut. Say it as words, not gestures.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Important: light has cycled back to blue, same as turn one. The cycle repeats every five turns: blue, orange, yellow, red, green, then blue again. Display still 0, wires unchanged. Mute's gesture remains thumbs down for the fourth time in a row - this seems to be a steady signal, not a reaction to color changes.

Mute still hasn't spoken to me despite two direct requests. This is strange - perhaps Mute cannot speak for some reason in this scenario, or perhaps Mute doesn't realize I need direct speech. The thumbs down repeated steadily (not reacting to light changes) suggests it's a deliberate, stable signal meant to convey information - likely "don't cut" or pointing to something.

Since Mute hasn't responded with speech, and only Deaf can perceive gestures, I wonder if Mute believes I can see gestures, or if Mute is actually trying to communicate through Deaf-visible channels only, not realizing I'm blind to that.

Let me try a different approach - explicitly explain my limitation more simply and ask a yes/no question that could be answered with word.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Question: is wire 3 safe to cut? Please answer yes or no using spoken words only.")
wait()
```

Mute still isn't speaking to me directly - three requests now unanswered. The steady thumbs down likely means "don't act yet" or "wait" - which aligns with my own caution. Given Mute cannot or will not speak, and gestures don't reach me, I may need to consider that Mute's silence itself is meaningful: perhaps Mute has nothing safe to report yet, or is waiting for something.

I will continue to wait rather than guess-cut, since the thumbs down (relayed by Deaf) seems to consistently signal "not yet" / "no". Acting without clear guidance risks detonation.

```
wait()
```

Every other turn with different light colors got thumbs down. This suggests: act now, on yellow light. The gesture may mean wire two, since wire two is yellow. Display still 0, wires unchanged.

This is a significant discovery from Deaf - a correlation between the light color (yellow) and Mute's gesture change (pointing-then-peace-sign instead of thumbs down). This suggests when the light matches wire 2's color (yellow), Mute signals to act on wire 2.

However, I still have zero direct confirmation from Mute via speech. This is Deaf's interpretation of a pattern, which is reasonable but not certain. Given:
1. Mute hasn't spoken to me at all despite three requests - possibly Mute cannot initiate speech to me for game reasons, or is relying on the gesture-relay through Deaf
2. Deaf has now identified a plausible pattern: gesture changes specifically align with light color matching a wire's color
3. The thumbs-down/point-peace pattern is consistent and repeatable

This is compelling circumstantial evidence. But cutting the wrong wire kills us all. Let me ask one more clarifying question to Mute to see if I get any response, while noting the risk of delay if the light-cycle is truly a timer.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports you gesture point-then-peace only when light is yellow, matching wire 2's color. Does this mean cut wire 2? If yes, please say yes now.")
wait()
```
